tasks.title: Review [architecture-agent] Implement When PRDs run The task bar should reflect in steps
tasks.description: Review pr-prd-when-prds-run-the-d8bef0-architecture-agent for Address review for [architecture-agent] Implement When PRDs run The task bar should reflect in steps
acceptance: Task `prd-when-prds-run-the-d8bef0-architecture-agent-1` is complete within the assigned agent scope.

The required wrapper check `npm run typecheck` passed and the branch appears mergeable with `origin/dev`, but the PRD step logic has a blocking correctness issue.
`src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/status-view.ts:158` marks the run as `reviewing` whenever any active PR exists, without checking whether the selected PRD still has unfinished tasks or whether the PR belongs to that PRD. The new unit test at `tests/unit/control-plane-dashboard.test.ts:148-155` codifies the bug by expecting `reviewing` while the active PRD is only 1/3 complete. This will make the task bar skip/misreport the implementing step for PRDs that still have remaining implementation work. Expected correction: keep PRDs with remaining tasks in `implementing`, and only move to `reviewing` when the current PRD's implementation work is complete or its current review PR is actually active. Add focused coverage for a partially completed PRD with an active PR remaining in `implementing`.

The required wrapper check `npm run typecheck` passed and the branch merge-tree against `origin/dev` showed no conflicts, but the prior blocking issue is still present. The latest commit only queues the review follow-up; it does not correct the PRD step logic.
`src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/status-view.ts:158` still returns `reviewing` whenever any pull request status exists, before checking whether the active PRD has remaining tasks or whether the PR belongs to that PRD. This keeps partially implemented PRDs from showing the `implementing` step accurately.
`tests/unit/control-plane-dashboard.test.ts:152` still asserts `prdRun.currentStepId` is `reviewing` for an active PRD with 1 of 3 tasks complete, codifying the incorrect behavior. Expected correction: keep PRDs with remaining implementation tasks in `implementing`; only move to `reviewing` once the active PRD's implementation work is complete or the active review PR is specifically for that PRD, and add focused coverage for the partial-PRD-with-active-PR case.

The wrapper check `npm run typecheck` passed and the branch merge-tree against `origin/dev` showed no conflicts, but the PR is not safe to approve because the actual branch HEAD still does not include the follow-up fix. The worktree has unstaged changes in the PRD step logic and tests; merging the branch would omit them.
Blocking merge-safety issue: `src/autonomy-v2/commands/shared-pr-status.ts`, `src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/status-view.ts`, and `tests/unit/control-plane-dashboard.test.ts` are modified only in the worktree. Commit these changes onto the PR branch before review/merge.
At committed HEAD, the prior blocker remains: `src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/status-view.ts` still moves to `reviewing` whenever any active PR exists, and `tests/unit/control-plane-dashboard.test.ts` still codifies that behavior for a partially complete PRD. The unstaged worktree changes appear to address this, and the focused built test passed, but those fixes are not mergeable until committed.

The required wrapper check `npm run typecheck` passed, the worktree is clean at the current PR branch HEAD, and a merge-tree check against `origin/dev` showed no conflicts. The prior uncommitted-worktree blocker is resolved, and the partial-PRD active-PR case is now covered. However, the committed implementation still does not reliably surface the `reviewing` step from real status snapshots.
Blocking correctness issue: `src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/status-view.ts:161` returns `implementing` whenever `completedTaskCount < plannedTaskCount`, but `completedTaskCount` only comes from `completedTaskSpecIds` in `describePrd` (`src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/status-view.ts:54`). Real status snapshots built by `loadTrackedPrds` do not populate `completedTaskSpecIds` at all (`src/autonomy-v2/commands/shared-prds.ts:75`), even though PR records carry completed/pending task state. As a result, a PRD with all planned implementation tasks in an open review PR will still render as `implementing` instead of `reviewing`, so the task bar does not reflect the review phase in the normal control-plane path.
Expected correction: derive completed task ids/counts in `loadTrackedPrds` from linked task statuses and/or the PR's `completedTaskIds`/`pendingTaskIds`, then make `resolvePrdRunStep` move the current PRD to `reviewing` when its implementation work is complete and its active PR/reviewer work is pending. Keep the existing partial-PRD-with-active-PR coverage, and add focused coverage that goes through the real snapshot path without manually injecting `completedTaskSpecIds`.

tasks.title: Review [architecture-agent] Implement PRD Control Plane package update and restart for managed repos
tasks.description: Review pr-prd-prd-control-plane-package-f7d2a3-architecture-agent for Address review for [architecture-agent] Implement PRD Control Plane package update and restart for managed repos
acceptance: Task `prd-prd-control-plane-package-f7d2a3-architecture-agent-1` is complete within the assigned agent scope.

`npm run typecheck` passed in the deterministic wrapper and the diff is lane-scoped, but the package update restart path is not safe to merge yet.
Blocking: `executeControlPlanePackageUpdate` runs restart commands before the bridge reports job completion. In `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-package-update.ts:10-15`, `runPackageUpdateRestartCommands` is called inside the update execution, and `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:150-184` only POSTs `/complete` after that returns. A real `controlBridgeRestartCommand` such as a pm2/systemd restart can terminate the current bridge process before it reaches `/complete`, leaving the job stuck as claimed and failing the acceptance requirement to complete with structured result data. Defer/detach the bridge self-restart until after the status and job completion are posted, or otherwise make completion durable before restarting the current process. Add focused coverage for this ordering; the current restart test uses a harmless child command and does not cover the self-restart hazard.

`npm run typecheck` passed in the deterministic wrapper and the diff is lane-scoped, but the round-1 blocker is still present. The package update path still executes restart commands before the bridge posts the updated status and `/complete` result, so a real bridge self-restart can terminate the current bridge process and leave the job stuck as claimed.
Blocking: `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-package-update.ts:10` calls `runPackageUpdateRestartCommands` inside `executeControlPlanePackageUpdate`, and `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:150` only posts repo status and `/complete` after that function returns. Defer or detach `controlBridgeRestartCommand` until after the status update and job completion are durably posted, or otherwise make completion durable before restarting the current bridge process.
Missing focused verification: `tests/unit/control-plane-package-update-bridge.test.ts:109` uses a harmless child process restart command, so it proves command execution but not the self-restart ordering hazard. Add coverage that asserts job completion/status reporting happens before any bridge self-restart command can stop the running bridge.

`npm run typecheck` passed in the deterministic wrapper and the diff remains lane-scoped, but the prior blocking restart-ordering issue is still present, so this is not safe to merge.
Blocking: `executeControlPlanePackageUpdate` still runs restart commands before the bridge posts the updated repo status and `/complete` result. `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-package-update.ts:10-15` calls `runPackageUpdateRestartCommands`, while `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:150-184` only posts status and completes the job after that call returns. A real `controlBridgeRestartCommand` can terminate/restart the running bridge before completion is durably reported, leaving the job stuck as claimed and violating the package update completion requirement. Defer/detach the bridge self-restart until after status and job completion are posted, or otherwise make completion durable before restarting the current bridge process.
Missing focused verification: `tests/unit/control-plane-package-update-bridge.test.ts:109-124` still uses harmless child-process commands, so it verifies command execution but not the self-restart ordering hazard. Add coverage that proves status reporting and job completion occur before any bridge restart command that could stop the active bridge process.

`npm run typecheck` passed in the deterministic wrapper, and the bridge restart is now deferred past the normal success path. Still blocking: the deferred self-restart is not tied to durable job completion, so the prior stuck-claimed-job failure mode can still happen on `/complete` failures.
In `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:173`, deferred bridge restart commands are queued before the job completion request. The completion POST at `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:199` is swallowed with `.catch(() => null)`, but the deferred restart still runs at `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:256`. If `/api/jobs/:id/complete` fails transiently, the bridge can restart itself while the job remains claimed, violating the package update completion requirement. Only launch deferred self-restart after completion is durably acknowledged, or drop the deferred restart and surface a failure when completion cannot be posted.
The focused deferral test in `tests/unit/control-plane-package-update-bridge.test.ts:109` covers the successful completion ordering, but it does not cover the completion-failure path. Add coverage proving a configured `controlBridgeRestartCommand` is not launched when `/complete` fails or cannot be acknowledged.
